$comment: An instance rather than a string, so the credentials inside a connection address are members a manifest reads and the runtime redacts, never text an author assembles. `members` gives the CEL fields, the object authoring form and per-member sensitivity in one declaration; `acceptsText` admits a CEL string at a slot of the type, read through the encoding when the resource holding it is created; the `scheme` parameter restricts the scheme member with a schema, while the member's CEL type stays `string`.
name: Telo.Url

host.description: The host: a name, an IPv4 address or an IPv6 address without its brackets. Present exactly when the URL has an authority, possibly empty.

port.description: The port number, when the URL names one.

user.description: The user name of the authority's user information.

password.description: The password of the authority's user information. Redacted wherever it is logged, as is the URL's whole text.

path.description: The path, unescaped (`/orders`). Absent when the URL has none.

query.description: The query as a map of each key to its value, unescaped. A key appears once.

parameters.name: scheme
parameters.description: A schema the scheme must satisfy (`scheme: { enum: [postgres, postgresql] }`). Omitted means any scheme.

description: A URL that may carry credentials, held as its members — scheme, host, port, user, password, path and query — each read in CEL as a field. Written as its text (`postgres://app:secret@db:5432/orders`) or as an object of members, which are escaped by RFC 3986 component rules, so a password holding `@` or `/` needs no hand escaping. The password and the whole text are redacted in logs; `string(url)` is its text.
